source.title: Commentary Critical and Explanatory on the Whole Bible
source.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset and David Brown
source.edition: CCEL expanded electronic edition of the 1871 public-domain text

entries.heading: Verse 1
entries.text: Ps 101:1-8 . In this Psalm the profession of the principles of his domestic and political government testifies, as well as actions in accordance with it, David's appreciation of God's mercy to him, and His judgment on his enemies: and thus he sings or celebrates God's dealings.
2. He avows his sincere purpose, by God's aid, to act uprightly ( Ge 17:1; Ps 18:30 ).

entries.heading: 3. set . . . eyes
entries.text: 3. set . . . eyes --as an example to be approved and followed. no wicked thing --literally, "word," plan or purpose of Belial ( Ps 41:8 ). work of . . . aside --apostates. not cleave to me --I will not be implicated in it (compare Ps 1:1-3 ).

entries.heading: 4. A froward heart
entries.text: 4. A froward heart --or, "perverse heart" ( Ps 18:26 ). Such a temper I will not indulge, nor even know evil or wickedness.
5, 6. The slanderers and haughty persons, so mischievous in society, I will disown; but--

entries.heading: 6. Mine eyes . . . upon
entries.text: 6. Mine eyes . . . upon --or, I will select reliable and honest men for my servants.

entries.heading: 7. not dwell
entries.text: 7. not dwell --literally, "not sit," or tarry, or be established.

entries.heading: 8. will early
entries.text: 8. will early --or, "diligently." city of the Lord --or, "holy place" ( Ps 48:2 ), where wicked men shall not be tolerated.
